title: Import my map
intro: Choose a global equirectangular heightmap, say how its grey values or numbers become metres, check the coast and height preview, and confirm. Nothing is created or changed before you confirm.

target.newHelp: On confirm a world is created from the chosen template and the heightmap is written into its geological input. If the import fails, the new world is removed again.
target.existingHelp: The heightmap is written into the geological input of the chosen world or branch and replaces its elevation. Reference worlds such as Earth have a read-only root; pick a branch that forks at the geological layer or earlier.
target.pickWorld: Choose the world to import into first.
target.noPlanet: This world has no planet to import into.
target.name: World name
target.nameHelp: Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores only, up to 64 characters; it is also the data folder name.
target.nameRequired: Enter a name for the new world.
target.nameInvalid: Use letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
target.nameTaken: A world named {{name}} already exists; choose another name.

template.earthlikeHelp: A rocky planet in the habitable zone of a G-type star, with an Earth-like atmosphere and rotation, ready for a climate run.
template.minimalHelp: A bare starting point; you fill in the star and planet parameters yourself.

help.file: Choose a 2:1 heightmap covering the whole planet, up to 4096 × 2048 pixels and 64 MiB. Use an equirectangular projection: the left and right edges are longitude −180° and +180°, and the top and bottom edges are the poles. Supported formats include 8-bit or 16-bit PNG, 16-bit TIFF, 32-bit float TIFF, and JPG (8-bit and lossy; the import report names the precision it costs).
help.regional: Regional map import is planned. It will require a latitude and longitude window and support local terrain refinement, not global climate calculations.
help.mapping: The same grey image can mean different things. Choose the description that fits this image, then fill in its numbers; the preview is recomputed from what you enter.
help.min_m: Height represented by the darkest value (0).
help.max_m_range: Height represented by the brightest value (full scale).
help.sea_level_m: Places above this height are land, the rest is sea. Usually 0 m.
help.sea_level: Grey value as a fraction of full scale, between 0 and 1. Pixels at or below it are sea; 0.05 makes the darkest 5% sea.
help.sea_level_grey: 0 is the darkest; grey levels at or below the threshold are sea. 0 makes only the darkest level sea; 1 also includes the next level.
help.max_m_threshold: Height of the brightest land. Land starts at 0 m on the coast.
help.seafloor_m: The image has no ocean depth, so every sea pixel gets this depth. It is an assumption and is recorded with the import.
help.curve: Linear maps grey to height evenly; a power curve makes lowlands flatter and mountains steeper.
help.gamma: Above 1 flattens lowlands; below 1 raises them faster.
help.notes: Optional: where the image comes from or what it is for; saved with the import record.
help.confirm: On confirm the original image and this declaration are saved in the world's geological input and the map elevation updates at once. Climate and other downstream results use the new terrain after the next build.

range.label: Grey includes the sea floor (range map)
range.desc: Black is the deepest sea floor, white the highest mountain, with heights in proportion between.

threshold.label: Only the land is drawn (threshold map)
threshold.desc: Everything below a grey value is sea and has no depth in the image; land rises from 0 m on the coast to the height of white.

metres.label: Values are already metres (float TIFF)
metres.desc: Pixel values are heights in metres; nothing is converted.

note.greyRange: 0 is the darkest, full scale is {{levels}} levels.

defaults.contract: Starting values are the import rule's defaults.
defaults.map: Starting values keep this map's current height scale.
defaults.request: The preview uses the values you entered.

view.sourceUnavailable: The browser cannot show this format (for example TIFF) directly. Use “Converted heights”.
view.sourceNote: The original is shown by the browser; 16-bit images appear as 8-bit grey here and cannot be read for values.

preview.hoverHint: Move the pointer over the preview to read latitude, longitude and height.
preview.gridNote: The preview is shown at {{w}} × {{h}}; the statistics below use the imported {{ow}} × {{oh}} raster.

report.landArea: Land share of the planet's surface
report.levelStepValue: {{coast}} m near the coast, up to {{max}} m
report.landNote: On an equirectangular map a pixel covers less ground nearer the poles, so the pixel share is not the planet's surface share. The surface share weights each row by its real area.
report.seafloorAssumed: The image has no ocean depth; all sea is set to {{depth}}. This is an assumption, not data.

warning.eightBit: This is an 8-bit image with only {{levels}} grey levels; one level is about {{coast}} m near the coast and up to {{max}} m. A 16-bit or float image is better.
warning.eightBitPlain: This is an 8-bit image with only 256 grey levels. A 16-bit or float image is better.
warning.jpegLossy: This is a JPG: 8-bit and lossy, so coastlines come out softer. Use the original PNG or TIFF when you have it.

diagnostic.range_all_sea: No pixel becomes land: the brightest source value covers {{brightest}} of full scale and maps to {{top}} m, below the sea level of {{sea}} m. If the brightest pixel is your highest peak, set white from {{white}} m to about {{suggested}} m (black stays {{black}} m).
diagnostic.range_all_sea_flat: No pixel becomes land: the source is a single flat tone, so a range mapping cannot create land. Use an image with light and dark tones, or switch to threshold mapping.
diagnostic.range_all_land: Every pixel is land: the darkest source value maps to {{bottom}} m, above the sea level of {{sea}} m. Set black below {{sea}} m, or raise the sea level above {{bottom}} m.
diagnostic.range_grey_use: The source uses only {{low}}–{{high}} of full scale; the brightest pixel maps to {{top}} m (pure white is {{white}} m). If the brightest pixel is your highest peak, set white to about {{suggested}} m (black stays as it is).
diagnostic.range_darkest_share: The darkest level ({{level}}/{{levels}}) covers {{share}} of the image. If those pixels are ocean and the brighter tones are land, threshold mapping (a land-only map) fits this image better.
diagnostic.threshold_all_sea: No pixel becomes land: the brightest source value covers {{brightest}} of full scale, at or below the sea threshold of {{thresh}}. Lower the threshold below {{brightest}}.
diagnostic.threshold_all_sea_grey: No pixel becomes land: the brightest pixel only reaches grey {{brightest}}/{{levels}}, at or below the sea threshold of {{thresh}}. Lower the threshold below {{brightest}}.
diagnostic.threshold_all_land: Every pixel is land: the darkest source value covers {{darkest}} of full scale, above the sea threshold of {{thresh}}. Raise the threshold to {{darkest}} or above.
diagnostic.threshold_all_land_grey: Every pixel is land: the darkest pixel is grey {{darkest}}/{{levels}}, above the sea threshold of {{thresh}}. Raise the threshold to {{darkest}} or above.
diagnostic.threshold_reach: The brightest pixel reaches {{reach}} m, {{share}} of the declared white height of {{white}} m. If it should be the highest point, set white to about {{suggested}} m.
diagnostic.metres_all_sea: No pixel becomes land: the highest source value is {{highest}} m, at or below the sea level of {{sea}} m. Check the source units or use an image with both land and sea.
diagnostic.metres_all_land: Every pixel is land: the lowest source value is {{lowest}} m, above the sea level of {{sea}} m. Check the source units or the sea level.

status.waitPreview: You can confirm once the preview matches what you entered.

error.maxAboveMin: The height of white must be above the height of black.
error.maxPositive: The height of white must be above 0 m.
error.seaLevelFraction: Enter a fraction from 0 up to (not including) 1.
error.seaLevelGrey: Enter a whole grey level between 0 and full scale.
error.seafloorNegative: The sea floor must be below 0 m.
error.previewFailed: The preview could not be made.
error.previewKeepsValues: Everything you entered is kept. The preview retries when you change a value or choose another file.
error.importFailed: The import did not finish; the world was not changed.
error.templateNoPlanet: Template {{template}} has no planet to import into.
error.aspect: This image is {{w}} × {{h}} pixels. Choose a whole-planet map exactly twice as wide as it is tall.
error.dimensions: This image exceeds {{w}} × {{h}} pixels. Downscale the global map while keeping its 2:1 aspect ratio.
error.fileSize: This file exceeds {{mib}} MiB. Downscale the image or export it with compression.
error.unreadable: The heightmap could not be read. Export a valid PNG, TIFF or JPG file and try again.

static.unavailable: The static site only browses published worlds; importing a map needs a local dreamulator serve.
